The `saveLocation` callers in the REST module are in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, not `openmrs-core`. The core `LocationService.saveLocation` is declared at `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/LocationService.java:68`, and its implementation is `LocationServiceImpl.java:67`.

**Confirmed affected (direct calls in the REST module)**

1. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/LocationResource1_8.java:218-224`. This is the `/ws/rest/v1/location` resource. Its `save(Location)` override, which the generic CRUD layer calls on create and update, returns `Context.getLocationService().saveLocation(location)` directly. Any change in return value, cascading, or validation reaches every location POST/update.
2. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/LocationAttributeResource1_9.java:85-103`. `save(LocationAttribute)` adds the attribute to its location and then calls `saveLocation(delegate.getLocation())` (line 101). A change in how `saveLocation` persists attributes affects `/ws/rest/v1/location/{uuid}/attribute` writes.
3. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/LocationAttributeResource1_9.java:109-114`. `delete` soft-deletes an attribute by setting it voided and then calls `saveLocation` (line 113). A change in how voided attributes are saved affects attribute retirement.

**Confirmed by inheritance (no direct call, but they run the code above)**

4. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/LocationResource1_9.java:32` extends `LocationResource1_8`. Unless it overrides `save`, which I did not read, it inherits the `saveLocation` path.
